title: Order Book Depth

statement.md: A market data handler rebuilds a depth-of-book view from a message stream. Each message either adds quantity at a price level or removes quantity from it. After the whole stream, print the **top $k$ price levels** on each side with their total resting quantity.

Bids are ordered from the highest price down, asks from the lowest price up. Levels whose quantity reaches zero disappear. A side with fewer than $k$ levels prints all it has, and an empty side prints `-`.

inputFormat: First line: $n$ and $k$. Then $n$ messages, one per line: `A side price qty` adds $qty$ at $price$ on `side` (`B` or `S`); `C side price qty` removes $qty$ from that level.
outputFormat: Two lines. The first starts with `BIDS`, the second with `ASKS`. Each is followed by up to $k$ levels written `price:qty` separated by spaces, or by `-` when the side is empty.
constraints: A remove never takes more than the level currently holds; level totals fit in 64 bits
hints: Keep one hash map per side from price to total quantity. Delete the key when the quantity reaches 0.
Sort only at the end: the whole stream costs O(n), and sorting the surviving levels costs O(L log L).

editorial.md: Aggregating as the stream arrives needs only a hash map per side. Only the final snapshot is requested, so the levels can be sorted once at the end. If you needed the top of book after every message, a sorted map or heap would be the right structure instead.
Deleting zero-quantity levels matters: a stale level with quantity 0 would show up in the depth and hide the next real level.
